exposure: presence of consultants on the labor ward
Consultant presence on labor ward ('in-hours' vs. 'out-of-hours')
cohort: Singleton live births at 19 obstetric units in the United Kingdom
finding: There was no significant difference in the rates of most maternal and neonatal morbidities between births that occurred 'in-hours' and 'out-of-hours', suggesting that the current organization of maternity care in the UK allows for good planning and risk management.
mod_finding: Women who delivered 'out-of-hours' had slightly lower rates of intrapartum caesarean section and instrumental delivery, and there was some evidence of a reduced rate of severe perineal tears in 'out-of-hours' vaginal deliveries.
